title: US markets closed — Thanksgiving Day (the gap this calendar carries a half-day for but no closure)
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) and its text layer decompressed stream-by-stream by the treasury-2y-note-2026-11-23 initial-research adjacency sweep. The schedule's own holiday line reads verbatim `Holiday - Thursday, November 26, 2026 - Thanksgiving Day`. Independently reproduced by statute and weekday arithmetic: 5 U.S.C. 6103 fixes Thanksgiving on the FOURTH Thursday in November, and the fourth Thursday of November 2026 is 2026-11-26. MECHANICALLY CORROBORATED FROM THE SCHEDULE'S OWN SETTLEMENT COLUMN, which does not depend on the holiday line: the 13-Week and 26-Week bills auctioned Monday 2026-11-23 settle `Friday, November 27, 2026`, and the 6-Week and 52-Week bills auctioned Tuesday 2026-11-24 settle the same Friday — Treasury moved the entire block's settlement off its standing Thursday because the market is shut. Filed estimate on the same counts the sibling closure entries labor-day-market-closure-2026-09-07, good-friday-market-closure-2027-03-26 and memorial-day-market-closure-2027-05-31 documented: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an exchange's or a trade association's own holiday calendar, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and no exchange calendar was reachable this session. The DATE is not in doubt — the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED 2026-09-09 by the treasury-2y-note-2026-11-23 initial-research adjacency sweep, which found it at D+3 inside the 5-day corridor. THE GAP IS ASYMMETRIC AND THAT IS WHY IT EARNS A ROW: this calendar already carries thanksgiving-half-day-2026-11-27 — the Friday early close — but no entry for the FULL closure the day before, so any window arithmetic keyed on tracked closures sees a shortened Friday floating with no holiday in front of it. The proposing sweep's own event depends on the fact: 2026-11-23 opens a coupon block compressed into Monday/Tuesday/Wednesday (2Y 11-23, 5Y + 2Y FRN 11-24, 7Y 11-25) precisely because Thursday is shut, and the Wednesday carries five macro releases (PCE, GDP-Q3-second, durable goods, new home sales, beige book) that a normal week would have spread across Thursday and Friday. MEASURED, so the entry is not just bookkeeping: across 2000-2026 par-curve sessions pulled 2026-09-09, the Monday/Tuesday/Wednesday of Thanksgiving week run mean |2Y move| 3.97bp against 3.62bp on all other sessions — the holiday week is NOT the quiet tape the intuition assumes, and the one session that stands out is the Tuesday (2 days before Thanksgiving), which closes -2.46bp on n=26 (t = -2.99) against a -0.03bp all-session mean. That is one incidental observation out of four offsets tested, not a claim. The sibling entry for the following year, if anyone files it, is 2027-11-25.
